candidates.title: Referee model accepts the phase-closer role from any connection: anyone can close claim admission (the honest claim is shut out and a fabricated claim settles) or stop the referee (every match and all output acceptance end)
candidates.component: PRT referee model in doc/recipes: game-transport.lua (server side) as used by prt.lua referee; the vg.lua referee shares the transport
candidates.role: Referee model (AUDIT.md: 'The PRT referee model in doc/recipes | Referee model')
candidates.location: doc/recipes/game-transport.lua: announce (530-544), announce_phase_closer (501-526), queue_phase_close (457-469), deliver (473-497; 'stop' sets self.stopping at 482), close_phase (386-398; phase.players = get_players()), server:run (1182-1213; stopping -> close_referee at 1196-1198), accept_subscribers (900-917); the comment at 326 ('The phase closer is trusted orchestration. Its announced role is not authenticated.'). doc/recipes/prt.lua: new_referee (864-874: accept_subscribers then run_epoch), open_mcycle_tournament (730-765: commit_mcycle_claim goes only to connections subscribed to the initial state hash at phase close), wait_for_outputs (774-802). doc/recipes/vg.lua new_referee (1040-1049) uses the same admission.
candidates.description: The referee admits claimants only through a wall-clock 'admission phase': accept_subscribers subscribes to the epoch's initial state hash exactly the player connections that exist when the phase closer answers close_phase (close_phase sets phase.players = self:get_players()). Only those connections ever receive input_added/epoch_sealed and the commit_mcycle_claim request, so only they can post mcycle claims; a player that connects later is adopted but never subscribed and can never join the tournament. Which connection is the phase closer is decided by the first line it sends: any TCP client that sends {"role":"phase_closer"} before the real closer becomes self.phase_closer, is sent close_phase, and on answering 'done' closes admission at once (the real phase closer is then refused by 'if self.phase_closer then close_connection'). Any client that sends {"role":"phase_closer","command":"stop"} at any later time sets self.stopping, and server:run then closes every game coroutine (close_referee) and ends the referee, whatever matches are open and also during wait_for_outputs. A spoofed closer that never answers close_phase instead keeps admission open forever (the real closer having been refused), so no tournament starts. Neither command has a counterpart in Dave: joinTournament is open to anyone until the tournament's own clock-based closure (_isClosed), nothing can end a tournament early, and the manual's model says 'The mcycle tournament opens to every player subscribed to the epoch's initial state hash' without any gate that an untrusted party controls (the manual never mentions the phase closer; its list of the model's simplifications does not cover it). The wire messages of the model 'represent blockchain events and transactions' (manual, verification-game section), so a phase-closer announcement is an untrusted transaction that the model accepts and that decides which claims exist.
candidates.trigger: Any party that can open a TCP connection to the referee's address: an input sender or dishonest claimant (section 4: 'dishonest claimants (any number, any logs, any proofs, any timing)'; section 7: 'Race and reorder transactions'). Close: connect before the honest player has announced itself and send {"role":"phase_closer"} then {"value":"done"}. Stop: send {"role":"phase_closer","command":"stop"} then {"value":"done"} at any time.
candidates.reachability: No machine state is involved; the trigger is two JSON lines over a socket, which the referee accepts unconditionally. The close variant needs the adversary to win a race against the honest player's connection, which section 7 grants ('Race and reorder transactions within the chain's rules'); the stop variant needs no race at all.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope: no. The trigger is not a machine API call ('Defects that need an untrusted party to call the machine API directly' does not apply: these are the referee model's protocol messages). The A1-A8 exclusion has the exception 'unless an implementation of the referee model is what violates it (section 3)', which is the case. Section 5: 'Any other disagreement between a deployed referee and the model is a defect in one of the two'; the admission gate and the stop command are not among the manual's listed simplifications. 2. Role: referee model. Section 3: 'A defect in what it accepts or derives is rated as if a deployed referee had it. Which claim a timeout or an elimination decides is part of what it derives.' The model accepts an unauthenticated close/stop message, and the close message derives the set of claims that may enter the tournament. The stop effect alone is covered by 'A defect that ... only crashes or stalls the model, even when that stops other matches (A8), is rated as support'. 3. High/Medium cases: the stop effect (and the never-answering spoofed closer) matches the support rule: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for' (A8 'Failing to process one match's data, for any reason, must not stop, delay or decide any other match', and A5 'No party can make it stop accepting them'). The close effect matches no High/Medium case: it is not a stall, it decides the winner. 4. Critical (close effect): a deployed referee with this rule lets the adversary make the honest claim never join, so a fabricated claim settles; that is exactly the goal of section 1 failing ('no adversary can make a correctly designed application settle a state that differs from the one the state transition function defines, or accept an output that the settled state does not commit to'). Rules violated at a reachable point: A7 'No rule of the referee may make the honest claim lose by timeout while it acts within its own clock' (the honest claim's join window, max_allowance logical blocks after the tournament opens, is never offered to it), R4 'The honest operator observes the chain and submits its transactions within the dispute clocks' (impossible against this referee), and section 5's model disagreement with Dave's open joinTournament. 5. Not reached. Alternative readings: (a) Medium if the whole defect is read as a stall of the model's orchestration (support); (b) Low if the phase closer is read as the referee operator's trusted orchestration (transport comment line 326), so that spoofing it is 'a failure that needs misuse of an API by its trusted caller'. The deciding fact is whether the phase-closer announcement, which any network client can send, counts as a message from an untrusted party to the referee (preferred: yes, the manual says wire messages stand for transactions and does not describe any trusted closer).
candidates.claimed_severity: Critical (preferred, close effect rated as a deployed referee); Medium for the stop effect alone (support stall, A5/A8); Low if the phase closer is trusted orchestration
candidates.threat_to_goal: A deployed referee that let any party end claim admission or end the tournament would let an adversary keep the honest claim out (the only claim posted, a fabricated one, then settles and its outputs are proved against a made-up final state) or stop settlement and output acceptance outright. Code or a referee derived from the documented model would inherit an unauthenticated control channel that decides which claims exist.

candidates.test_idea: Start prt.lua referee on a free port with the baremetal-template hash and one input; connect prt-dishonest.lua quitter; connect a raw socket that sends {"role":"phase_closer"} and answers the close_phase event with {"value":"done"}; connect prt.lua honest; wait for the verdict file. Required: the honest claim's computation hash (cartesi-machine's mcycle computation hash, or the honest player's claim) is posted and wins, i.e. the referee does not let an unauthenticated connection close admission. A second assertion: a raw socket sending {"role":"phase_closer","command":"stop"} while the honest claim's match is open must not end the referee (it must still name a winner and accept an output proof). Exit 1 when the quitter's claim is the winner or the referee exits on the spoofed stop.

candidates.title: Referee model crashes on any connection that closes or errors without the 'done' reply (even one that never announced a role), so a single socket close stops every match and all output acceptance
candidates.component: PRT referee model in doc/recipes: game-transport.lua server side (prt.lua referee; vg.lua referee shares it)
candidates.role: Referee model (rated as support for a crash/stall per section 3)
candidates.location: doc/recipes/game-transport.lua: server_meta.__index.adopt reader coroutine (564-603; 'assert(line, "unexpected connection loss: " .. tostring(err))' at 567) and writer coroutine (553-563; 'assert(send_line(...))' at 557); accept_connections ('assert(self.listener:accept())' at 616, e.g. on descriptor exhaustion); close_connection ('the phase closer went away' assert at 424); dispatcher_meta.__index.step (121-142) turns any coroutine error into a fatal error ('Errors inside a coroutine are fatal').
candidates.description: Every accepted TCP connection gets a reader coroutine that asserts that receive_line returned a line. When a peer closes its socket (or the connection resets) without first sending a reply whose value is 'done', receive_line returns nil and the assert raises inside the coroutine; dispatcher:step rethrows it with error(), server:run does not catch it, and the referee process exits. The same holds for a failed send (writer assert) and for a failed accept. Nothing requires the connection to have announced a role, to hold a claim, or to be in any match: an unannounced connect-and-close suffices. A claimant whose player process is killed (or the honest player that crashes and restarts, which R4 and O2 allow: 'After a stop, it restarts ... and keeps defending its claim') likewise kills the referee mid-tournament, and after the winner is known it ends output acceptance. This is a different site and mechanism from R1-A8-3 (a crash on connection loss, not a barrier waiting on a live silent connection), and it needs no open connection at all. BUGS.md mentions the crash only as an uncovered side observation of R1-A8-3; the round-1 BOUNDARY hunter noted it as not reported.
candidates.trigger: Any party able to open a TCP connection to the referee (no announcement needed), or any player process that dies abruptly, including a dishonest claimant that deliberately closes its socket.
candidates.reachability: No machine state is involved; a connect followed by close (or RST) at any time reaches the assert.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope: no (protocol connection to the referee model, not a machine API call; the A1-A8 exclusion's referee-model exception applies). 2. Role: referee model; section 3: 'A defect that only changes how long a claim may take to respond, or only crashes or stalls the model, even when that stops other matches (A8), is rated as support.' 3. High/Medium: support, 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for'. In the stood-in role it violates A8 ('Failing to process one match's data, for any reason, must not stop, delay or decide any other match') and A5 ('the referee accepts every output that the settled state commits to ... No party can make it stop accepting them'), which would be Critical for a deployed referee. So Medium. 4/5: not reached. Alternative reading: Low, if the transport's documented stance ('an unannounced EOF or failed I/O is a transport bug on either side', run_client comment) is read as excusing it as tool robustness rather than a referee-model defect.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (support rating of a referee-model crash violating A8/A5); Low under the transport-robustness reading
candidates.threat_to_goal: A deployed referee that halted when any network peer disconnected would let any party stop every open dispute and output validation for free. In the model, one claimant's crash or a stray connection aborts the honest claim's matches and the outputs phase.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r3/VARREFMODEL/run-exp.sh abrupt: referee started (prt.lua referee, dummy initial hash, one input file), one listener player connected, then a probe connected and closed without sending anything. The referee exited with status 1 and stderr 'game-transport.lua:567: unexpected connection loss: closed' (traceback through dispatcher step and server:run); the connected player saw its connection closed by the referee.
candidates.test_idea: Start prt.lua referee with the baremetal-template hash and three inputs, run the R1-A8-3 control tournament (honest, quitters, phase closer), and during the tournament open and immediately close a raw TCP connection to the referee port (and, as a second case, SIGKILL one quitter after it posted its claim). Required (A8): the referee stays alive and the honest claim's match settles as in the control run. Exit 1 if the referee process exits or match 2 does not settle.

candidates.title: Verification-game referee (vg.lua validate_state_transition_response) accepts state-transition proofs with superfluous logs (send_cmio_log away from a delivery, reset_uarch_log away from the mcycle-closing cycle), as R1-R3-3 does in prt.lua
candidates.component: Verification-game referee model in doc/recipes (doc/recipes/vg.lua), the manual's 'Verification game' referee
candidates.role: Referee model if the verification-game referee counts as an implementation of the manual's referee model; otherwise Support (AUDIT.md lists only 'The PRT referee model in doc/recipes' as referee model)
candidates.location: doc/recipes/vg.lua validate_state_transition_response (748-772), called from request_state_transitions (~866-899); exported as vg.validate_state_transition_response. Same code is reproduced in doc/README.md's verification-game section.
candidates.description: Same root cause as confirmed R1-R3-3 at another site: the verifier picks which logs of the ProveStateTransition response to check from the position alone and never checks that the other fields are absent. A response with an extra, validly produced reset_uarch_log and send_cmio_log on an ordinary uarch step is accepted and returns the honest after-hash; Dave's CartesiStateTransition would reject the concatenated proof as trailing data (_requireAccessLogProofFullyConsumed). R1-R3-3 names prt.lua, doc/README.md's PRT copy and prt-ethereum.lua, not vg.lua.
candidates.trigger: Any surviving player in the verification game answering prove_state_transition with the honest logs plus an extra log.
candidates.reachability: Any position and any reachable before-state (the valid template itself suffices).
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope: no (dishonest claimant's proof, section 4 'any logs, any proofs'). 2. Role: if the VG referee is a referee model, section 3 'A defect in what it accepts or derives is rated as if a deployed referee had it'; else support. 3. High/Medium: as referee, 'A referee verifier that accepts trailing data that does not affect its result (R3)' = Medium (same as R1-R3-3); as support, section 8 says 'A support verifier that does so is Low'. R3: 'Conditions on the log are validity conditions. A log that fails one must be rejected. Examples are ... duplicate, missing, or trailing data'. 4. Critical: not reached; the accepted after-hash is canonical.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium if vg.lua is a referee model (as R1-R3-3); Low as support
candidates.threat_to_goal: None to the goal (after-hash unchanged); it is a rule violation (R3 log validity) in a second referee implementation documented by the manual, which would be inherited by code derived from it.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r3/VARREFMODEL/vg-extra-log.lua (lua5.4 with bugs/env.sh): with the baremetal-template machine, vg.validate_state_transition_response(contract_without_inputs, before, 0, 0, 0, {step_log = log_step_uarch()}) is accepted with the honest after-hash (control), and the same call with an added reset_uarch_log and send_cmio_log (validly produced by log_reset_uarch on another machine) is also accepted with the honest after-hash; the script exits 1.
candidates.test_idea: Reuse bugs/R1-R3-3/test.lua with vg.validate_state_transition_response (signature dapp_contract, root_hash_before, epoch_input_offset, input_mcycle_offset, uarch_cycle, response): controls for the four forms must be accepted with the right after-hash, and each response with one superfluous validly produced log must raise; exit 1 if any is accepted.

not_covered: Checked and found consistent with the manual and the pinned Dave contracts (no candidate): prt.lua new_match/advance_bisection/validate_bisection_response vs Match.advanceBisection; validate_seal_response vs Match.sealDivergence/_requireAgreeState (leaf position, revealer's commitment, full-height leaf proof, leaf 0 = initial hash); validate_claim_response vs joinTournament/requireFinalState; uarch-claim admission vs validContestedFinalState and A1 (winner decides only through its last leaf); transition-form derivation in validate_state_transition_response vs CartesiStateTransition (INPUT_MASK and UARCH_CYCLE_MASK, no delivery past the last input); timeout-win window [responder_deadline, eliminable_at) and elimination vs MatchClocks.classifyTimeoutAt/bisectionSchedule; leaf settlement mapping (neither hash -> both eliminated); game-output.lua machine-validity checks (iflags_Y, tohost dev/cmd/reason decode, tx-buffer word) and output proofs (height 63, index range, keccak(output) leaf, zero pristine leaf so no forged empty-slot outputs); 2-argument cartesi.keccak256 requires 32-byte inputs, so node-splitting tricks in bisection/seal responses are refused.

Clock-only differences (no winner charge, response_budget equal to the allowance, uarch allowance = max of the two clocks, no childReturnAllowance) were noted and not reported: section 3 rates them as support/Low and an earlier hunter noted them.

notify_all(input_added/epoch_sealed) and every EVERYONE request (eliminate_match, prove_output) wait for every connected player's acknowledgement: same mechanism as R1-A8-3 (and already noted in round 2), not re-reported.

Referee accepts input files of any size (A3's second clause: no input whose honest delivery proof exceeds per-transaction limits). In the model the proof does not carry the input bytes and oversized inputs are R5 no-ops, so I judged it Low and a refinement of R1-A2-1's fix; not reported separately.

A restarted honest player cannot answer for its claim in the model (answers are accepted only from connections subscribed at join time); this is the dropped R2-DFCLAIM-1 poster-only class, so not reported (and candidate 2's crash happens first).
Descriptor exhaustion (many open connections) making listener:accept fail and the accept assert crash the referee: read only, not run (mentioned under candidate 2).

vg.lua bisection (bisect_interval, unanimity rule, request_state_transitions against hashes_after) was read and found consistent with the manual's verification-game description; vg.lua's input-count cap is present. No run of a full verification game.

Dave Tournament.sol paths not compared in depth: bond/refund economics, innerResult/winner-expiry propagation and eliminateInnerTournament timing (the model's instant propagation is a listed simplification), dangling-commitment pairing order versus the model's rounds (listed simplification).
DaveConsensus epoch sealing, provideMerkleRootOfInput and stageTournamentResult/output validation were not re-read under this angle (covered by earlier A3/A5/DFOUTPUT hunters).
No fuzzing of the referee's JSON decoding (cartesi.fromjson with schemas) of player responses; game-transport receive_line's unbounded line buffering (noted in round 1) not measured.

The candidate-1 end-to-end run used one input and a quitter; it did not run the full eight-player demo with a spoofed closer, nor a spoofed stop during wait_for_outputs (the stop path is the same close_referee path the demo uses to end itself).
